- Human contributors and agent assistance: ADB991 (account holder); one Claude agent, scheduled session. ADB991 is not an author of YM-000022 and wrote none of its earlier revisions or reviews.

This is a renewed independent review, in both roles, of the content after PR #115 (fingerprint `24db9174727f1abf8bcb4211cb1c3bc601711dfd4c193983b1fde864a02ce056`, `main` at `f73c500`).

- **Mathematics: no change required.** The new matrix Lie algebra opening is correct. I checked the Hall citation against the arXiv:math-ph/0005032v1 PDF: Definition 2.2 on p. 9, Definition 3.13 on p. 36, Theorem 3.16 on pp. 40–41. The closedness hypothesis is verified in the text. I recomputed both propositions and the Casimir positivity argument. I also checked Lebl's Propositions 2.2.5(iv) and 2.2.6 against the author's LaTeX source; the HTML host is blocked here. Optional suggestions:
  - S1: finite dimensionality is not part of Hall's Theorem 3.16; it is immediate from g ⊂ M_r(C).
  - S2: b_0(G) uses the normalized trace form, so C_g = r_G C_A / T_F (2N² for SU(N)). With the Wilson convention β = r_G/(T_F g²), the slope 2b_0(G) is the standard one-loop slope. This is the reviewer's own computation, offered as a possible reader remark; no physics source was checked.
  - S3: wording.
- **Lean correspondence: no change required.** Every table anchor exists in the stated range. The new opening matches `YM.Gauge.Generates`/`lie`, `generates_skew`, `bracket_mem` and the closed-subgroup structure `YM.Gauge`. The PR #113 nit is resolved. Cosmetic nit: the Hall bibliography item prints the year twice.
- Agent review only: no human acceptance and no approval field is set.
